text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bunds came under pressure in late trade with the prospect of fresh supply from a new 10-year issue due on Tuesday. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.44, down 0.38 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts failed to shrug off the gloom that infected European bonds markets and settled down 10/32 down on the day. All European bonds markets fell on expectations that French President Jacques Chirac would later today announce early parliamentary elections in order to push through austerity measures. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-15/32, down 09/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - The French debt market and the franc tumbled further, extending last week's losses, ahead of a snap general election expected to be called later in the evening by President Jacques Chirac. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.28, down 0.44 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures were lower ahead of the data from the first six Italian cities reporting preliminary April CPI, when CPI inflation is expected to dip under two percent. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.37, down 0.39 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were a bit weaker at midday, as the market started to build in some concessions ahead of note auctions later this week. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-29/32, down 03/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.07 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher due to short-covering by dealers. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.94, down 0.01 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Activity in the Eurobond market was very limited, with only a handful of small transactions seen. Merrill Lynch brought a self-led 100 million stg bond. Telecom Corp of New Zealand tapped the Swiss franc sector for the first time with a 150 million franc bond. A number of deals were expected this week. In dollars, NTT and BGB were likely to issue $500 million five-year deals. Spain's 2.0 billion Ecu-euro bond was also due this week. In marks, Porsche said it would issue a bond soon.
